t: Given kₚ for the reaction 1/2C(g)⇌1/2A(g)+1/2B(g) at a fixed temperature is 0.25 atm⁻². Find the Kₚ for the reaction A(g)+B(g)⇌C(g) at the same temperature.
s:
For the reaction,
1/2C(g)⇌1/2A(g)+1/2B(g)
Given, Kₚ=0.25 atm⁻² We know that, K_C=([ Product ]ᵇ)/([ Reactant ]ᵃ), where a and b are stiochiometric coefficients. Also, Kₚ=K_C(RT)^(Δn_g) where, Δn_g=b−a For above reaction, K_(C₁)=([A]^(0.5)[B]^(0.5))/([C]^(0.5))
Δn_g=1−0.5=0.5
So,
K_(p₁)=K_(C₁)(RT)^(0.5)...(i)
Similarly for reaction, A(g)+B(g)⇌C(g), at same temperature
[K_(C₂) =([C])/([A][B]); Δn_g =1−2=−1; K_(p₂) =K_(C₂)(RT)⁻¹...(ii)]
Now, divide K_(p₁) and K_(p₂), we get,
(K_(p₁))/(K_(p₂))=(K_(C₁)[RT]^(0.5))/(K_(C₂)[RT]⁻¹)⇒K_(p₂)=16 atm
So, Kₚ for the reaction
A(g)+B(g)⇌C(g) is 16 atm.
p: Law of Mass Action, Equilibrium Constant (Kc and Kp) and its Application

t: Consider the expression ΔG=−RTlnKₚ+RTlnQₚ and indicate the correct statement:
s:
ΔG=−RTlnKₚ+RTlnQₚ=RTln(Qₚ/Kₚ)
When Qₚ<Kₚ: Qₚ/Kₚ<1 → ln(Qₚ/Kₚ)<0 → ΔG<0 → reaction shifts forward (left to right).
When Qₚ=Kₚ: Qₚ/Kₚ=1 → ln(Qₚ/Kₚ)=0 → ΔG=0 → system at equilibrium.
When Qₚ>Kₚ: Qₚ/Kₚ>1 → ln(Qₚ/Kₚ)>0 → ΔG>0 → excess products, reaction shifts in reverse (right to left).
p: Law of Mass Action, Equilibrium Constant (Kc and Kp) and its Application
o: ΔG=0,Qₚ>Kₚ the equilibrium reaction will shift from left to right
ΔG=0,Qₚ=Kₚ the equilibrium reaction will shift from left to right
ΔG=∞,Qₚ<Kₚ the equilibrium reaction will shift from right to left
ΔG>0,Qₚ>Kₚ the equilibrium reaction will shift from right to left

t: In which of the following reactions, the equilibrium remains unaffected on addition of small amount of argon at constant volume?
s: Noble gas or inert gas does not react itself due to the extremely low reactivity of noble gas with other substances. As Ar is a noble gas, it is also unreactive but it decreases the activation energy in both forward as well as backward directions by the same amount of reversible reaction. When Ar is added at constant volume, the equilibrium will not change as there is no change in the no. of moles of the reaction (forward and backward) of either reactant or products. ⇒H₂(g)+I₂(g)⇌2HI(g) ⋅ No. of moles for forward reaction =2 for reactant and 2 for product ⋅ No. of moles for backward reaction =2 for reactant and 2 for product ⇒PCl₅(g)⇌PCl₃(g)+Cl₂(g) ⋅ No. of moles for forward reaction =2 for reactant and 1 for product ⋅ No. of moles for backward reaction =1 for reactant and 2 for product ⇒N₂(g)+3H₂(g)⇌2NH₃(g) ⋅ No. of moles for forward reaction =4 for reactant and 2 for product ⋅ No. of moles for backward reaction =2 for reactant and 4 for product Hence, in all cases equilibrium remains unaffected. Conclusion: Therefore, the equilibrium will remain unaffected in all three cases. Hence, the correct answer is option 4.
p: Le chatelier’s principle
o: The equilibrium will remain unaffected in all the three cases.

[[img:a98af0c80017]]
s: Given the options: 1. Pressure has no effect: This is incorrect because pressure does affect the equilibrium of reactions involving gases. 2. P₁<P₂<P₃ : If pressure increases, the yield of the product SO₃ should increase. Therefore, this would mean that P₁ (lowest pressure) has the lowest yield, P₂ (intermediate pressure) has a higher yield, and P₃ (highest pressure) has the highest yield. 3. P₁>P₂>P₃ : This implies that the yield decreases with increasing pressure, which is contrary to what we expect. 4. P₁=P₂=P₃≠0 : This would imply that pressure has no effect on the yield, which contradicts Le Chatelier’s Principle. Conclusion: The correct option is: (2) P₁<P₂<P₃ This means that as pressure increases, the yield of SO₃ increases.
p: Le chatelier’s principle

The expression of K_C would be free from concentration term only when value of x is 2 . Putting x=2, gives
